papers.title: EsViritu is a sensitive and specific profiler for viral pathogen detection and genome recovery in metagenomes.
papers.abstract: Metagenomic sequencing allows for detection of any number of pathogenic viruses from a single sample without a priori knowledge of its contents. This has created a substantial opportunity to characterize pathogens in humans and their environment, but the field is held back by a lack of bioinformatics tools for taxonomic profiling and reconstructing virus genomes. The ideal profiler would simultaneously do two things: report viruses at single-read sensitivity so that ultra-low-abundance pathogens are not missed and hold near-perfect specificity so that a pathogen is never falsely reported. Here
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: EsViritu is a new bioinformatics tool for detecting and reconstructing viral genomes from metagenomic sequencing data. It aims to achieve both single-read sensitivity (so even ultra-low-abundance viruses are detected) and near-perfect specificity (so no false positives are reported), addressing a key gap in viral pathogen profiling.

papers.title: Evaluation of Parallel Accumulation-Serial Fragmentation methods for metaproteomics using a model microbiome.
papers.abstract: We present a multi-organism, ground-truth metaproteomic dataset generated using data-dependent acquisition Parallel Accumulation-Serial Fragmentation (ddaPASEF) and data-independent acquisition (diaPASEF) on a trapped ion mobility mass spectrometer. The dataset comprises 28 species (30 strains) spanning Archaea, Bacteria, Eukarya, and bacteriophages, assembled into an uneven mock community with a 400-fold dynamic range of organismal abundance. Four biological replicates were processed using a standardized sample preparation workflow and analyzed using described LC-MS conditions. Raw data, sear
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This paper introduces a multi-organism ground-truth metaproteomic dataset from a 28-species mock microbiome spanning Archaea, Bacteria, Eukarya, and bacteriophages with a 400-fold dynamic range, analyzed using both ddaPASEF and diaPASEF on a trapped ion mobility mass spectrometer. The resource enables benchmarking of parallel accumulation-serial fragmentation acquisition methods for metaproteomics, with four biological replicates and standardized sample preparation.

papers.title: Genome-resolved ecology and evolution of the microbiome enabled by quantitative long-read metagenomics.
papers.abstract: Standard metagenomics resolves microbial communities only in relative terms and at coarse taxonomic resolution, obscuring how individual strains change in absolute abundance and evolve within a host. We present long-read quantiomics (LRQ), a quantitative metagenomics platform coupling long-read sequencing with plasmid-based internal standards to recover high-quality genomes, including from degraded or low-input stool, and measure absolute, genome-resolved strain abundances. We validate LRQ using large plasmid standards and bacterial spike-ins, then apply it to eight years of dense sampling fro
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The authors present long-read quantiomics (LRQ), a metagenomics platform that combines long-read sequencing with plasmid-based internal standards to recover high-quality genomes and measure absolute, genome-resolved strain abundances, even from degraded or low-input stool samples. They validate the method with plasmid standards and bacterial spike-ins, then apply it to eight years of dense longitudinal sampling to track how individual strains change in absolute abundance and evolve within a host. This enables genome-resolved ecological and evolutionary analysis of the microbiome that relative-abundance methods cannot provide.

papers.title: Mediation Analysis with Compositional Exposures.
papers.abstract: Understanding the causal pathways linking the gut microbiome to downstream biomarkers and clinical outcomes is central to microbiome research. When the microbiome acts as the exposure, the high dimensionality and compositional structure of the data introduce unique methodological challenges for mediation analysis. To address these challenges, we propose a latent variable mediation framework that captures variation in microbial composition through a microbial balance, defined as the log-ratio between two unknown subsets of taxa. This balance serves as a latent scalar exposure and simplifies the
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The paper proposes a latent variable mediation framework for microbiome studies where the exposure is compositional (relative abundance) and high-dimensional. It models microbial composition via a 'microbial balance'—the log-ratio of two unknown taxa subsets—as a latent scalar exposure, simplifying mediation analysis of pathways from the microbiome to downstream biomarkers and clinical outcomes.

papers.title: New genetic tools in Finegoldia magna identify a conserved adhesin required for the formation of stress-tolerant aggregates.
papers.abstract: The Gram-positive obligate anaerobe Finegoldia magna is a member of the healthy human microbiota, but also acts as an opportunistic pathogen to cause persistent, biofilm-associated infections. Despite its prevalence on the human host, little is known about F. magna biology or the mechanisms underlying its clinically relevant phenotypes, partly due to the lack of genetic tools. We address this gap by establishing genetic approaches for investigating gene function in F. magna , which we apply to identify genetic determinants of aggregate biofilm formation. We found that F. magna isolates are nat
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This preprint establishes new genetic tools for Finegoldia magna, a common human skin and mucosal bacterium that can also cause persistent biofilm infections. Using these tools, the authors identify a conserved adhesin protein that is required for the bacteria to form stress-tolerant aggregates, providing a first handle on the molecular basis of biofilm formation in this understudied organism.

papers.title: Heat-Inactivated Lacticaseibacillus paracasei PC-01 Alleviates DSS-Induced Colitis in Mice by Modulating Gut Microbiota and Intestinal Barrier Function.
papers.abstract: Background: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is a chronic, progressive, immune-mediated inflammatory disorder of the gastrointestinal tract. Methods: This study used C57BL/6J mice induced by DSS to construct an intestinal inflammation model, and explored the alleviating effect and potential mechanism of heat inactivated Lactobacillus paracasei PC-01 (PC-01) on intestinal inflammation. Results: The results showed that heat-inactivated PC-01 significantly decreased the Disease Activity Index and H&E histopathological scores (p < 0.05). It also reduced the serum levels of pro-inflammatory cytokin
papers.summary: This study shows that heat-inactivated Lacticaseibacillus paracasei PC-01 reduces colitis severity in DSS-treated mice, lowering disease activity and histopathology scores and decreasing serum pro-inflammatory cytokines. The protective effect appears to work through modulation of the gut microbiota and improvement of intestinal barrier function, suggesting that non-viable probiotic preparations may have therapeutic potential for IBD.

papers.title: Metagenomic analysis of developmental-category-associated fungal communities in the gut contents of Achatina fulica, an intermediate host of Angiostrongylus cantonensis.
papers.abstract: The invasive giant African snail (Achatina fulica) poses serious agricultural and ecological threats and serves as an important intermediate host of the zoonotic parasite Angiostrongylus cantonensis, which causes human eosinophilic meningitis. While its gut bacterial microbiome has been extensively characterized, the gut mycobiome remains largely uncharacterized. In particular, variations in gut fungal communities across developmental stages remain unknown, limiting our understanding of the A. fulica gut holobiont.
papers.summary: This study uses metagenomic sequencing to characterize the fungal communities (mycobiome) in the gut contents of the giant African snail Achatina fulica across different developmental stages, a host that transmits the parasite causing human eosinophilic meningitis. It provides the first description of how gut fungal community composition varies with snail development, complementing prior work on the bacterial microbiome and advancing understanding of the snail gut holobiont.

papers.title: From Prediction to Mechanism: Explainable AI for Plant-Microbiome Multi-Omics Integration and Biological Discovery.
papers.abstract: Predicting complex phenotypes from plant-microbiome multi-omics data has advanced significantly with machine learning and deep learning. However, traditional black-box models remain limited by their focus on predictive performance rather than mechanistic biological understanding. To bridge this gap, explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) has emerged as a key framework to transform biological data analysis from correlation mapping to hypothesis-driven discovery. This review synthesizes current advances in XAI methodologies, including post hoc feature attribution techniques and intrinsically
papers.summary: This review synthesizes explainable AI (XAI) approaches for integrating plant-microbiome multi-omics data, arguing that black-box predictive models must be complemented by interpretability methods to move from correlation to mechanistic insight. It surveys post hoc feature attribution techniques and intrinsically interpretable models, framing XAI as a bridge between prediction and hypothesis-driven biological discovery.

papers.title: Gut Microbiota Signatures Associated with Metastatic Prostatic Cancer Treated with Androgen Receptor Pathway Inhibitor (ARPI) Therapy.
papers.abstract: Metastatic prostate cancer (MPCa) remains an aggressive disease despite the introduction of androgen receptor pathway inhibitors (ARPIs), and biomarkers predicting progression are still lacking. The aim of this study was to investigate gut microbiota (GM) composition and functional potential associated with advanced disease and progression under ARPI therapy. The GM of 15 patients with metastatic PCa receiving ARPIs, including 5 patients with disease progression, was compared with that of 39 patients with untreated (UT) PCa using shallow shotgun metagenomic sequencing. The metastatic PCa cohor
papers.summary: This study compared the gut microbiota of 15 metastatic prostate cancer patients receiving androgen receptor pathway inhibitors (ARPIs) with 39 untreated prostate cancer patients using shallow shotgun metagenomic sequencing. The authors identified distinct microbial composition and functional signatures associated with metastatic disease and with progression under ARPI therapy, suggesting the gut microbiome may hold potential as a biomarker for treatment response. The small sample size (only 5 progressors) means these findings are preliminary and require validation in larger cohorts.

papers.title: Evolution of lake microbial structure and function under climatic and anthropogenic forcings: Insights from sedimentary ancient DNA.
papers.abstract: Structure and function of lake microorganisms are sensitive to environmental disturbances; yet their differential responses to climatic and anthropogenic forcings over centennial scales remain poorly understood. Here, we analyzed a sediment core from Lake Daihai in northern China, combining metagenomics and stable isotope analyses. Our results revealed that microbial community assembly was dominated by deterministic processes, whereas stochasticity increased notably after 1850, coinciding with the termination of the Little Ice Age and intensified human impacts. Notably, microbial community str
papers.summary: Using sedimentary ancient DNA and stable isotopes from a Lake Daihai sediment core in northern China, the authors reconstructed how lake microbial community structure and function responded to climatic and human pressures over centuries. They found that deterministic assembly processes dominated historically, but stochasticity rose sharply after 1850, coinciding with the end of the Little Ice Age and intensifying anthropogenic impacts. The work links centennial-scale environmental change to shifts in microbial community assembly and function.

papers.title: Integrated In Silico Analysis Reveals ABC Transporter ATP-Binding Protein as a Therapeutic Target in Helicobacter pylori.
papers.abstract: Helicobacter pylori remains a major cause of gastric diseases, while increasing antimicrobial resistance highlights the need for novel therapeutic targets. Here, we developed a comprehensive computational target-prioritization framework integrating Rosetta Stone domain-fusion analysis, subtractive genomics, metabolic pathway mapping, structural modeling, and molecular dynamics simulations to identify pathogen-specific drug targets in H. pylori J99. Twelve conserved domain families comprising 746 proteins were identified, and domain abundance showed a weak negative correlation with versatility
papers.summary: This study uses a computational pipeline combining domain-fusion analysis, subtractive genomics, metabolic pathway mapping, structural modeling, and molecular dynamics to prioritize drug targets in Helicobacter pylori J99. The authors identify an ABC transporter ATP-binding protein as a promising pathogen-specific therapeutic target, supporting it with structural and simulation evidence. The work is entirely in silico and would require experimental validation.

papers.title: Synergistic effect of gastric microbiome and host genetic factor predispose to gastric cancer.
papers.abstract: Complex interaction between host genetic and environmental factors has a role in Helicobacter pylori (H. pylori)-related gastric tumorigenesis, while involvement of non-Helicobacter pylori gastric microbiome may be also relevant to this process. We aimed to evaluate whether combining the non-Helicobacter pylori gastric microbiome signatures and the gastric cancer (GC) predisposing genetic factors (PSCA rs2294008 and MUC1 rs4072037 polymorphisms) stratify a high GC risk subpopulation in a Japanese cohort.
papers.summary: This study examined whether combining non-Helicobacter pylori gastric microbiome signatures with two known gastric cancer risk polymorphisms (PSCA rs2294008 and MUC1 rs4072037) can identify a high-risk subpopulation in a Japanese cohort. The authors report that the gastric microbiome and host genetic factors act synergistically, with the combination stratifying individuals at elevated gastric cancer risk better than either factor alone.

papers.title: A global atlas of the gut virome reveals subtype-specific and functional alterations in irritable bowel syndrome.
papers.abstract: The gut virome is a critical component of the microbiome-gut-brain axis; however, its role in irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) remains poorly understood due to limited sample sizes and geographic bias. We aimed to construct a comprehensive global atlas of the IBS gut virome to elucidate its composition, functional potential, and clinical relevance across diverse populations and IBS subtypes. We integrated multi-cohort data comprising 1,104 samples (790 IBS patients and 314 healthy controls) from 11 cohorts across 10 geographic regions. A standardized bioinformatic pipeline was employed to perfor
papers.summary: This study integrates gut virome data from 1,104 samples across 11 cohorts and 10 geographic regions to build a global atlas of the gut virome in irritable bowel syndrome (IBS). The authors identify subtype-specific virome alterations and functional differences between IBS patients and healthy controls, addressing prior limitations of small sample sizes and geographic bias. The work highlights the gut virome as a relevant component of the microbiome-gut-brain axis in IBS.

papers.title: Association of quantitative sputum Candida load with respiratory dysbiosis and airway inflammation in suspected invasive pulmonary candidiasis.
papers.abstract: The clinical significance of Candida species isolation from sputum remains ambiguous due to the colonization-infection dilemma. Integrating quantitative culture with microbiome profiling may clarify its role, yet systematic evidence is scarce. In this exploratory study (June 2023-June 2026), we enrolled 140 hospitalized patients suspected of invasive pulmonary candidiasis (IPC) and stratified them into possible IPC (n = 36), probable IPC (n = 71), and negative control (n = 33) groups based on clinical criteria. All underwent quantitative fungal culture of sputum and metagenomic next-generation
papers.summary: This exploratory study of 140 hospitalized patients with suspected invasive pulmonary candidiasis combined quantitative sputum fungal culture with metagenomic next-generation sequencing to examine how Candida burden relates to respiratory microbiome disruption and airway inflammation. Patients were stratified into possible, probable, and negative control groups, allowing the authors to test whether higher quantitative Candida loads track with dysbiosis and inflammatory markers. The work aims to clarify the long-standing colonization-versus-infection dilemma for sputum Candida isolates.

papers.title: Breastfeeding and maternal microbial reservoirs are associated with infant gut phageome development during the first year of life.
papers.abstract: The early-life assembly of the gut microbiome is a critical determinant of long-term health, yet the role of bacteriophages in this process remains poorly understood. Here we longitudinally profile the gut phageome of 34 mother-infant dyads during the first year of life with metagenomics and a phage-centered computational workflow. Phage diversity increases with age, paralleling bacterial diversification but following distinct ecological trajectories. Shared viral populations across maternal and infant samples are consistent with potential maternal contribution, although not indicative of dire
papers.summary: This study tracked the gut phageome (the community of viruses that infect bacteria) in 34 mother-infant pairs over the first year of life using metagenomics. Phage diversity increased with infant age, following a different ecological path than bacteria, and shared viral populations between mothers and infants suggest possible maternal transmission. Breastfeeding and maternal microbial reservoirs were associated with how the infant phageome developed.

papers.title: Identifying low-quality features and suboptimal models to enhance phenotype prediction.
papers.abstract: It is common to build predictive models for complex phenotypes, such as diseases, where sample sizes are often limited by the cost of data collection. Machine learning and statistical methods are widely used in these cases. However, they may fail to identify high-quality features and lead to suboptimal models with high underfitting or overfitting risks. Here, we present mBoost to identify low-quality features and suboptimal models to enhance phenotype prediction. Importantly, it provides confidence on model performance, helping researchers avoid the frustrating cycle of model switching for pos
papers.summary: The authors introduce mBoost, a method for identifying low-quality features and suboptimal models in phenotype prediction, where limited sample sizes make overfitting and underfitting common. mBoost provides confidence estimates on model performance, helping researchers avoid repeatedly switching models without clear justification. This addresses a practical pain point in building predictive models for complex diseases with costly data collection.

papers.title: Effects of probiotics on joint homeostasis and osteoarthritis: Development of microbe-gut-cartilage axis-on-a-chip.
papers.abstract: Although emerging evidence implicates gut microbiome-cartilage cross-talk in the pathogenesis of osteoarthritis (OA), the most common joint disease, studying this microbe-gut-joint axis remains challenging due to limitations of animal models and conventional in vitro systems. Here, we report a microbe-gut-cartilage axis-on-a-chip (MGCAoC) that recreates tissue-specific microenvironments with oxygen gradients and physiological fluid shear. The computer simulation-optimized chip design generates an anoxic-oxic interface for the gut module and enables perfusion of probiotic metabolites to human c
papers.summary: The authors developed a microbe-gut-cartilage axis-on-a-chip (MGCAoC) that recreates the oxygen gradients and fluid shear of the gut-joint system, enabling study of how probiotic metabolites affect human cartilage. This platform provides a new way to investigate the gut microbiome's role in osteoarthritis, which has been difficult to study with animal models or conventional in vitro systems.

papers.title: Beyond Taxonomy: Fungal Nutraceutical Supplementation Modifies the Functional Potential of the Gut Microbiome in Colorectal Cancer.
papers.abstract: The gut microbiome is increasingly recognized as an important determinant of host immune regulation, intestinal homeostasis, and recovery after colorectal cancer (CRC) surgery. Although our previous randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial demonstrated that fungal nutraceutical supplementation with Micodigest® was associated with favorable taxonomic and systemic inflammatory changes in patients undergoing CRC surgery with curative intent, the functional consequences of this intervention remain poorly understood. Here, we performed a functional metagenomic analysis of fecal s
papers.summary: This study extends a prior randomized placebo-controlled trial by analyzing the functional metagenomic potential of gut microbiome samples from colorectal cancer surgery patients who received a fungal nutraceutical supplement (Micodigest®). Rather than focusing only on which microbial taxa changed, the authors examine shifts in functional gene content, suggesting the supplement may alter microbiome functional capacity relevant to host immune and inflammatory responses. The work moves beyond taxonomic description toward understanding what the microbiome is functionally capable of doing after intervention.

papers.title: Deciphering the heterogeneity of prodromal α-synucleinopathy: linking brain biotyping and gut dysbiosis in isolated REM sleep behaviour disorder.
papers.abstract: Isolated/idiopathic REM sleep behaviour disorder (iRBD) is a specific prodrome of α-synucleinopathies. We previously identified two distinct clinical-neuroimaging biotypes in iRBD: Biotype 1, marked by widespread cortical-subcortical-cerebellar atrophy with motor and cognitive deficits, and Biotype 2, with preserved brain structure and neurocognition. Converging evidence implicates the gut-brain axis in early α-synucleinopathy, yet its role in these divergent iRBD phenotypes remains unexplored.
papers.summary: This study examines whether the two previously identified brain biotypes of isolated REM sleep behaviour disorder (iRBD)—one with widespread brain atrophy and cognitive/motor deficits, the other with preserved brain structure—differ in gut microbiome composition. By linking brain biotyping with gut dysbiosis, the authors aim to show that gut-brain axis alterations may underlie the heterogeneity of this prodromal α-synucleinopathy. The work connects neuroimaging phenotypes to microbial signatures in a prodromal Parkinson's disease context.

papers.title: Integrated multi-omics and metabolic modeling links structure to function in high-performing electrosynthetic biofilm communities.
papers.abstract: Microbial electrosynthesis (MES) is a promising technology for the valorization of CO2 into industrially relevant building blocks. The high-performing MES systems in terms of production rates of acetate (12.5-19.7 mmol L-1catholyte day-1), butyrate (1.9-12.2 mmol L-1catholyte day-1), and caproate (0.6-0.9 mmol L-1catholyte day-1) discussed in this study consist of mixed microbial communities. However, the microbial community members, metabolic pathways, and interactions driving product formation in MES communities remain poorly understood. To overcome these challenges, we conducted a comprehen
papers.summary: This study integrates multi-omics data with metabolic modeling to characterize mixed microbial communities in high-performing microbial electrosynthesis (MES) systems that convert CO2 into acetate, butyrate, and caproate. By linking community structure to metabolic function, the authors identify the key community members, pathways, and interactions driving product formation. The work provides a framework for understanding and potentially optimizing electrosynthetic biofilm communities.

papers.title: Novel Antarctic chemolithotroph drives iron biomineralization.
papers.abstract: Iron, the most abundant redox-active metal in the Earth's crust, is coupled to numerous biogeochemical cycles. However, the mechanisms of iron oxidation and the organisms involved remain incompletely understood. Banded iron formations (BIFs) are a major reservoir of iron ore in the Precambrian sedimentary record, yet the biological contribution to their genesis remains a subject of unresolved debate. While large-scale BIF deposition largely ceased after the Proterozoic, microbial activity in modern Holocene sediments under fluctuating redox conditions provides a unique opportunity to examine m
papers.summary: This study characterizes a novel Antarctic chemolithotrophic microorganism that oxidizes iron and drives iron biomineralization, offering a modern analog for understanding how microbes may have contributed to ancient banded iron formations. By examining microbial activity in Holocene sediments under fluctuating redox conditions, the authors provide new insight into the biological mechanisms of iron oxidation and mineral deposition.

papers.title: Escherichia coli-derived enterobactin is associated with delayed gut microbiome maturation in infants born to mothers with obesity.
papers.abstract: Maternal obesity has been increasingly recognized as a factor influencing early-life microbiome development. However, its impact on the infant gut resistome and virulome remains insufficiently characterized. In this prospective longitudinal study, we investigated gut microbiome composition, antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs), and virulence factor profiles in infants born to mothers with obesity and normal weight during the first year of life. Shotgun metagenomic sequencing was performed on maternal and infant fecal samples collected at birth and at 1, 3, 6, and 12 months. Infants born to obese
papers.summary: This prospective longitudinal study used shotgun metagenomic sequencing to track gut microbiome composition, antibiotic resistance genes, and virulence factors in infants born to mothers with obesity versus normal weight over the first year of life. The key finding is that Escherichia coli-derived enterobactin is associated with delayed gut microbiome maturation in infants of mothers with obesity, linking maternal obesity to altered early-life microbiome development and resistome/virulome profiles.

papers.title: Mallard super-shedders of avian influenza exhibit distinct cloacal microbial abundance profiles.
papers.abstract: In many infectious disease systems, a small fraction of hosts accounts for a disproportionate share of transmission, but the biological basis of this heterogeneity remains poorly resolved. In avian influenza, mallards show substantial variation in viral shedding, raising the possibility that only a subset of individuals contributes strongly to environmental contamination and onward spread. To examine whether host microbiome structure is associated with this variation, we experimentally infected wild, captive mallards with low-pathogenic avian influenza virus. We characterized cloacal microbiom
papers.summary: This study experimentally infected wild-caught mallards with low-pathogenic avian influenza and characterized their cloacal microbiomes, finding that individuals with the highest viral shedding (super-shedders) had distinct cloacal microbial abundance profiles compared to lower shedders. The results suggest that host microbiome structure may be associated with heterogeneity in viral shedding and transmission potential.

papers.title: Early-Life Gut Microbiota and the Pediatric Gut-Lung Axis: A Systematic Review of Clinical, Preclinical, and Mechanistic Evidence.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: The early-life gut microbiota plays a pivotal role in immune maturation and may influence respiratory health through the gut-lung axis. However, evidence linking microbial development, dysbiosis, microbial metabolites, and microbiota-targeted interventions to pediatric respiratory outcomes remains heterogeneous. This systematic review aimed to synthesize clinical and preclinical evidence on the pediatric gut-lung axis and its underlying mechanisms. Methods: This systematic review followed PRISMA 2020 guidelines and a prospectively registered PROSPERO protocol (CRD4202510
papers.summary: This systematic review synthesizes clinical and preclinical evidence on how the early-life gut microbiota influences pediatric respiratory health via the gut-lung axis, covering microbial development, dysbiosis, metabolites, and microbiota-targeted interventions. The authors find the evidence heterogeneous but supportive of a role for gut microbial maturation in immune programming and respiratory outcomes. It consolidates mechanistic hypotheses and highlights gaps for future pediatric research.

papers.title: Patterns of Functional Redundancy and Anaerobic Metabolic Potential Characterise the Skin Microbiome of a Critically Endangered Sawfish.
papers.abstract: Using shotgun metagenomics of largetooth sawfish (Pristis pristis) skin and paired pool water samples, we provide the first taxonomic and functional characterisation of a sawfish skin microbiome and assess its ecological distinctiveness, assembly, and resilience relative to the surrounding water column. The skin microbiome was strongly host-associated and compositionally distinct, with lower taxonomic richness than the water column but dominated by Bacillota, particularly spore-forming Bacilli. Functional profiling revealed genes associated with sporulation, dormancy, anaerobic metabolism, and
papers.summary: This study provides the first taxonomic and functional characterization of the skin microbiome of the critically endangered largetooth sawfish using shotgun metagenomics. The skin microbiome is strongly host-associated and distinct from the surrounding water, dominated by spore-forming Bacillota, and enriched for genes related to sporulation, dormancy, and anaerobic metabolism. These patterns suggest functional redundancy and adaptive strategies that may help the microbiome persist under environmental stress.

papers.title: Subclinical Mastitis and Antibiotic Exposure Reshape the Milk Bacteriome, Resistome, and Metabolic Functional Profiles in Dairy Cows.
papers.abstract: Subclinical mastitis (SCM) reduces milk yield and promotes antibiotic use, contributing to antimicrobial resistance. However, information on milk microbiome dysbiosis and resistome alterations in dairy cows remains limited. We performed shotgun metagenomic sequencing of 30 milk samples from 20 cows classified as SCM (n = 10), antibiotic-treated (ANT; n = 10), and healthy milk (HM; n = 10). Bacteriome, resistome, and metabolic functions were analyzed using bioinformatic tools. Microbial alpha diversity was significantly higher in HM than SCM and ANT samples (p < 0.05), with the greatest richnes
papers.summary: Shotgun metagenomic sequencing of milk from dairy cows showed that subclinical mastitis and antibiotic treatment both reduce microbial diversity compared with healthy milk, and reshape the bacteriome, antibiotic resistance gene (resistome) content, and metabolic functional profiles. The study links mastitis and antibiotic exposure to milk microbiome dysbiosis and altered resistance potential, highlighting a need for more judicious antibiotic use.

papers.title: Genotype-dependent phosphorus acquisition responses of two soybean genotypes under combined low phosphorus and salt stress: evidence from root traits, exudates and rhizosphere microbiome.
papers.abstract: Soil salinization and phosphorus (P) deficiency often co-occur in coastal saline-alkali soils, severely limiting crop productivity. Although root exudates are known to mediate rhizosphere microbiome assembly, the coordinated associations among root exudates, rhizosphere microbes, and P acquisition under combined salinity stress and phosphate deficiency remain unclear. In this study, we used two salt-tolerant soybean genotypes differing in P efficiency (A74, P-efficient; A6, P-inefficient) as materials. In a controlled pot experiment, four treatments were established: control (CK), low P (LP),
papers.summary: This study compares two salt-tolerant soybean genotypes that differ in phosphorus-use efficiency (A74 efficient, A6 inefficient) grown under combined low-phosphorus and salt stress, examining root traits, root exudates, and rhizosphere microbiome composition. The work aims to clarify how exudate-microbe-root coordination drives genotype-dependent phosphorus acquisition under these co-occurring stresses. It provides evidence that P-efficient genotypes mount distinct rhizosphere responses linking exudation and microbiome assembly to better P uptake.

papers.title: Association of microbial pathways predicted/inferred using 16S and shotgun metagenome with faecal metabolite abundances.
papers.abstract: The gut microbiome is an essential metabolic organ influencing host health through metabolite production. While metabolite production levels can be directly measured by gas or liquid chromatography, they are commonly inferred from the abundance of metagenomic functional pathways. To evaluate the accuracy of these inferences, we established a single, manually curated metabolite-pathway/enzyme mapping list as a standardized biological reference. We then compared liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS)-based faecal metabolites with functional pathways/enzymes inferred from four approaches
papers.summary: This study tests how accurately gut microbial metabolite production can be inferred from metagenomic pathway predictions rather than measured directly. The authors built a manually curated metabolite–pathway/enzyme mapping reference and compared LC-MS faecal metabolite abundances against functional predictions from 16S and shotgun metagenome approaches. The work provides a standardized benchmark for evaluating the reliability of pathway-based metabolite inference.

papers.title: Targeted genome recovery of under-sequenced microbes from the Sequence Read Archive STAT.
papers.abstract: Most microbial species are represented by a single genome in public databases. The lack of genomes for these 'singleton' organisms limits our understanding of their pan-genome diversity and evolution. Although the Sequence Read Archive (SRA) contains millions of sequencing datasets that could be used to expand our understanding of many species, the extent to which under-represented microbial species are present at levels sufficient for genome recovery is unclear. Here, we show that the pre-computed taxonomic profiles generated by the National Center for Biotechnology Information SRA Taxonomy A
papers.summary: The authors show that NCBI's pre-computed SRA Taxonomy Analysis Tool (STAT) profiles can be used to identify under-sequenced microbial species that are present at sufficient abundance in public sequencing datasets to allow targeted genome recovery. This enables expansion of genome coverage for 'singleton' microbes without new sequencing, leveraging the vast SRA archive.

papers.title: Genome-resolved metagenomics reveals rare taxa and functional traits in two contrasting agricultural fields.
papers.abstract: Agricultural soils harbor highly diverse and functionally rich microbial communities, yet much of their genomic potential remains unexplored. Here, we present a genome-resolved metagenomic analysis of 455 soil samples collected at different depths and seasonal stages across two Danish agricultural fields representing sandy and clay soil types. Ultra-deep shotgun sequencing enabled the recovery of 58 831 medium to high-quality prokaryotic metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs), which were dereplicated into 56 340 strain-level MAGs and 9090 species-level genome bins (SGBs) spanning 49 prokaryotic p
papers.summary: This study performed ultra-deep shotgun metagenomic sequencing on 455 soil samples from two Danish agricultural fields with contrasting soil types (sandy vs. clay), recovering 58,831 medium- to high-quality prokaryotic MAGs that dereplicated into 56,340 strain-level genomes and 9,090 species-level genome bins across 49 phyla. The analysis highlights rare taxa and functional traits that differ between soil types and depths, substantially expanding the genomic catalog of agricultural soil microbiomes.

papers.title: To cohabit or inoculate? Testing the limits of microbiota transplantation in Manila clams.
papers.abstract: Microbiota transplantation has emerged as a powerful tool to investigate host-microbe interactions across a wide range of organisms, yet its applicability and ecological limits in marine bivalves remain poorly understood. Here, we experimentally test whether microbiota associated with chronic environmental contamination can be transferred and persist in adult Manila clams (Ruditapes philippinarum). We compared two water-mediated approaches: (i) inoculation of a donor tissue homogenate into the water and (ii) cohabitation with live donor clams through shared seawater flow. Donors originated fro
papers.summary: This study tested two methods for transferring gut microbiota between Manila clams: adding a donor tissue homogenate to the water versus cohabiting donor and recipient clams in shared seawater. The goal was to see whether microbiota from chronically contaminated environments could be transferred and persist in adult clams. The results help define the practical and ecological limits of microbiota transplantation experiments in marine bivalves.

papers.title: Metagenomic insights into the pulmonary microbiome of drug-sensitive and multidrug-resistant tuberculosis patients.
papers.abstract: While the pulmonary microbiota may influence TB pathogenesis, direct comparisons between drug-sensitive (DS-TB) and multidrug-resistant (MDR-TB) patients remain scarce. This study explored microbiome differences between these groups.
papers.summary: This study compared the pulmonary microbiome of patients with drug-sensitive versus multidrug-resistant tuberculosis using metagenomic sequencing. It identifies microbial community differences associated with resistance status, suggesting the lung microbiota may play a role in TB pathogenesis or treatment outcomes. The work provides a baseline for future studies on microbiome-TB interactions.

papers.title: Strategies for modelling the intestinal mucus interface: Focus on drug transport and host-microbiota interactions.
papers.abstract: The intestinal mucus barrier is a complex, dynamic hydrogel that plays a central role in host-microbiota interactions, nutrient transport, and protection against pathogens. Understanding its physicochemical properties has become essential for developing predictive in vitro and in silico models for drug delivery, microbiome research, and disease modelling. Over the past decade, advances in polymer chemistry, glycoscience, and microfluidics have enabled the development of increasingly sophisticated mucus models that mimic structural, rheological, and biochemical features of native intestinal muc
papers.summary: This review surveys strategies for modelling the intestinal mucus barrier, a dynamic hydrogel central to drug transport and host-microbiota interactions. It highlights how advances in polymer chemistry, glycoscience, and microfluidics have enabled increasingly sophisticated in vitro and in silico mucus models that mimic native structural, rheological, and biochemical features. The paper aims to guide selection of predictive models for drug delivery, microbiome research, and disease modelling.

papers.title: Root canal microbiota in diabetic versus non-diabetic patients with apical periodontitis: A systematic review.
papers.abstract: This systematic review aimed to evaluate the differences in root canal microbiota composition and microbial load between diabetic and non-diabetic individuals with apical periodontitis.
papers.summary: This systematic review compares the composition and load of root canal microbiota in diabetic versus non-diabetic patients with apical periodontitis. It synthesizes available evidence to determine whether diabetes alters the microbial community in infected root canals, which could influence disease severity and treatment outcomes.

papers.title: TSLC: differential abundance analysis method for identifying biologically relevant known microbes.
papers.abstract: Identifying biologically relevant microbes is a crucial task in human microbiome studies. Numerous computational and statistical methods have been proposed for this task. However, most existing methods are based solely on taxonomic information, even when whole-metagenome sequencing data are available, and thus cannot account for the fact that different microbes can perform the same or similar functions (known as functional redundancy) and for the contribution of unknown microbes to functional abundance. Hence, the identified differentially abundant microbes might not be biologically relevant t
papers.summary: The paper introduces TSLC, a differential abundance analysis method for microbiome studies that incorporates functional information from whole-metagenome sequencing rather than relying solely on taxonomic profiles. This allows the method to account for functional redundancy among microbes and the contribution of unknown taxa, aiming to identify microbes that are more biologically relevant. The approach addresses a key limitation of existing taxonomic-only methods.

papers.title: Effects of cultivation of herbaceous perennials on soil microbial community structure and nitrogen cycling functions.
papers.abstract: This study aimed to elucidate the impacts of cultivating different herbaceous perennials on the rhizosphere microenvironment, nitrogen-cycling microbial communities, and functional genes in black soils of urban green spaces in Northeast China, thereby providing a scientific basis for rational urban plant configuration and interspecific differences in soil nutrient cycling. Focusing on five commonly utilized herbaceous perennials in Changchun (Lycopus lucidus [P-LL], Salvia japonica [P-SJ], Hemerocallis fulva [P-HF], Hosta ensata [P-HE], and Pseudolysimachion spicatum [P-PS]), this study integr
papers.summary: The study compares how five herbaceous perennial species grown in urban green spaces in Northeast China affect rhizosphere soil microbial community composition and nitrogen-cycling functional genes. It finds species-specific differences in microbial community structure and nitrogen cycling potential, suggesting that plant selection can shape soil nutrient cycling in urban landscapes.

papers.title: Beyond community state types: vaginal microbial diversity and CST-IV signatures are associated with pregnancy in euploid embryo transfer cycles.
papers.abstract: Despite significant progress in assisted reproductive technology, in vitro fertilization (IVF) pregnancy rates remain suboptimal. Although the vaginal microbiome has been implicated in IVF outcomes, prior studies often overlooked embryonic aneuploidy, a major confounder. This study aimed to investigate the association between the vaginal microbiome and pregnancy outcomes in euploid embryo transfer cycles.
papers.summary: This study examined the vaginal microbiome in women undergoing IVF with euploid embryo transfers, removing chromosomal abnormalities as a confounder. It found that vaginal microbial diversity and specific CST-IV signatures were associated with pregnancy outcomes, suggesting the microbiome influences IVF success beyond embryo genetics.

papers.title: Effects of trait stacking on the maize phyllosphere microbiome: a shotgun metagenomic comparison.
papers.abstract: Current safety assessments for stacked-trait transgenic crops underrepresent the phyllosphere, a critical interface directly exposed to transgenic products, warranting strengthened risk evaluation. Here, we employed metagenomics to characterize the phyllosphere of three maize lines under herbicide-free conditions: wild-type (Corn.CK), herbicide-resistant single-trait (transgene of cp4-epsps, Corn.S), and insect- and herbicide-resistant stacked-trait (transgene of cry1Ab and cp4-epsps, Corn.D). Shannon diversity showed a consistent trend toward higher values in the cp4-epsps single-trait line t
papers.summary: This study used shotgun metagenomics to compare the phyllosphere microbiome of three maize lines: wild-type, a single-trait herbicide-resistant line (cp4-epsps), and a stacked-trait line (cry1Ab + cp4-epsps), all grown without herbicide. Shannon diversity trended higher in the single-trait line, suggesting that trait stacking may alter phyllosphere microbial community composition. The work argues that current transgenic crop safety assessments underrepresent the phyllosphere and should include microbiome evaluation.

papers.title: CRC-TrustBench: benchmarking cross-study and cross-country generalization in gut metagenomic colorectal cancer prediction.
papers.abstract: Gut metagenomic classifiers for colorectal cancer (CRC) are often evaluated with random splits that place samples from the same studies, countries, or processing workflows in both training and test sets, potentially inflating apparent performance. We developed CRC-TrustBench, a leakage-aware framework for evaluating cross-study and cross-country generalization and probability reliability.
papers.summary: CRC-TrustBench is a benchmarking framework that evaluates gut metagenomic colorectal cancer classifiers under leakage-aware, cross-study and cross-country conditions rather than random splits. It shows that conventional random-split evaluation can inflate apparent performance and adds assessment of probability reliability. The work provides a more realistic standard for judging whether CRC metagenomic classifiers generalize beyond their training cohorts.

papers.title: A genome-resolved cyanobacterial consortium from the Atacama Desert reveals novel bacterial diversity, stress-resilience potential, chromatic flexibility, and photoprotection.
papers.abstract: The Atacama Desert is one of the most extreme terrestrial environments on Earth, characterized by hyper-aridity, intense solar and ultraviolet radiation, oxidative stress, and metal-rich substrates. Here, we characterized an enriched cyanobacteria-associated consortium obtained from a high-altitude, river-influenced site in Quebrada Talabre, Atacama Desert. Deep shotgun metagenomic sequencing, achieving 99.7% estimated community coverage, enabled the reconstruction of 14 high-quality metagenome-assembled genomes representing five bacterial phyla. Genome-resolved analyses revealed multiple puta
papers.summary: The authors used deep shotgun metagenomic sequencing to characterize a cyanobacteria-associated microbial consortium from an extreme high-altitude site in the Atacama Desert, reconstructing 14 high-quality metagenome-assembled genomes spanning five bacterial phyla. Genome-resolved analyses revealed novel bacterial diversity and genomic features suggesting stress resilience, chromatic flexibility, and photoprotection mechanisms adapted to hyper-arid, high-UV conditions.

papers.title: High-throughput sequencing reveals the virome characteristics of wastewater in Gansu Province, China from 2024 to 2026.
papers.abstract: Emerging and re-emerging infectious diseases continue to pose a persistent challenge to global public health security. As an unbiased and noninvasive population-level surveillance approach, wastewater-based epidemiology has emerged as an urban-scale monitoring tool for proactively capturing the community disease burden. In this study, metagenomic and targeted next-generation sequencing were employed to preliminarily characterize wastewater viral communities in Gansu Province from 2024 to 2026. Across the three annual sampling groups, the Simpson diversity index calculated from metagenomic taxo
papers.summary: This study used metagenomic and targeted next-generation sequencing to characterize viral communities in wastewater across Gansu Province, China, over 2024–2026. It provides a preliminary survey of the wastewater virome, including diversity metrics across annual sampling groups, supporting wastewater-based epidemiology as a population-level surveillance tool. The work is largely descriptive and region-specific.

papers.title: Altered gut microbial functional landscape in children with pediatric inflammatory multisystem syndrome following SARS-CoV-2 infection: an exploratory metagenomic study.
papers.abstract: Pediatric Inflammatory Multisystem Syndrome (PIMS), also known as MIS-C (Multisystem inflammatory syndrome in children), is a severe post-infectious inflammatory condition associated with SARS-CoV-2 in children. While coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19), caused by SARS-CoV-2, primarily affects the respiratory system, growing evidence highlights gastrointestinal involvement and the relevance of the gut-lung axis in systemic inflammation. However, the taxonomic and, particularly, the functional landscape of the gut microbiome in children with PIMS remains insufficiently characterized.
papers.summary: This exploratory metagenomic study characterizes the gut microbiome of children with Pediatric Inflammatory Multisystem Syndrome (PIMS/MIS-C) following SARS-CoV-2 infection, focusing on functional rather than just taxonomic profiles. It finds an altered gut microbial functional landscape in these children, supporting a role for the gut-lung axis in post-COVID systemic inflammation. As an exploratory study, it provides a foundation for larger investigations into microbiome-mediated mechanisms in PIMS.

papers.title: Cervicovaginal microbiome alterations across HPV infection.
papers.abstract: The cervicovaginal microbiome is a proposed modifier of HPV-associated cervical disease, yet its relationship with viral type heterogeneity, cytological grade, and community state type (CST) remains incompletely understood.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
papers.summary: This study examines how the cervicovaginal microbiome differs across HPV infection status, viral type, and cytological grade, aiming to clarify whether specific bacterial community state types are associated with HPV-related cervical disease. The findings suggest that microbiome composition may modify HPV-associated risk, though the abstract does not report specific results.

papers.title: Dynamic changes in gut microbiota of three breeds of stud boars pre- and post-amoxicillin administration.
papers.abstract: Amoxicillin is a commonly used broad-spectrum antibiotic in pig farming, valued for its cost-effectiveness and efficacy in addressing prevalent swine ailments. However, the specific effects on the gut microbiota of stud boars and the trajectory of microbial recovery post-antibiotic withdrawal remain insufficiently elucidated.
papers.summary: This study tracked gut microbiota changes in stud boars from three breeds before and after amoxicillin administration, characterizing how the antibiotic perturbs the microbial community and how it recovers after withdrawal. It provides breed-specific insight into antibiotic-induced dysbiosis in an understudied livestock population.

papers.title: Prebiotic dietary fibers, gut microbiota, and short-chain fatty acid production: from fermentation mechanisms to clinical translation.
papers.abstract: The importance of the gut microbiota in regulating host homeostasis, immune responses, metabolism, and dietary interactions is increasingly recognized. Short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs), microbial metabolites produced through the fermentation of dietary substrates, play a central role in mediating these interactions. Drawing on mechanistic evidence from in vivo studies and insights from in vitro host-microbe fermentation models, this review critically examines how prebiotic dietary fibers have influenced the human gut microbial ecosystem, fermentation pathways, and SCFA production over the past
papers.summary: This review examines how prebiotic dietary fibers are fermented by gut bacteria to produce short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs), which mediate host-microbe interactions affecting metabolism, immunity, and homeostasis. It synthesizes mechanistic evidence from in vivo studies and in vitro fermentation models to trace pathways from fiber intake to SCFA production and discusses clinical translation.

papers.title: IMicAP: an intelligent microbial application platform for knowledge-driven microbiome research.
papers.abstract: Microorganisms play a pivotal role in health and disease, yet microbial research is hindered by fragmented data, heterogeneous knowledge representation, and a lack of integrated analytical tools. Existing databases and knowledge graphs often focus narrowly on genomic information, leaving critical metabolomic and literature-based associations underdeveloped.
papers.summary: IMicAP is presented as an integrated platform designed to unify fragmented microbial data, including genomic, metabolomic, and literature-derived associations, into a knowledge-driven resource for microbiome research. The platform aims to overcome the limitations of existing narrow databases by offering integrated analytical tools for exploring microbial associations with health and disease.

papers.title: Potential involvement of a TLR4-associated CD155/TIGIT pathway in Porphyromonas gingivalis-induced immunosuppressive microenvironment formation in oral squamous cell carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Accumulating evidence indicates that oral microbiota dysbiosis and periodontal pathogens contribute to the initiation and progression of oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC). However, the molecular mechanisms underlying the interaction between Porphyromonas gingivalis and the tumor immune microenvironment remain incompletely understood. This study aimed to investigate the potential role of a TLR4-associated ERK/CD155/TIGIT signaling pathway in P. gingivalis-mediated immunosuppressive microenvironment formation during OSCC progression.
papers.summary: This study investigates how the periodontal pathogen Porphyromonas gingivalis may promote an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment in oral squamous cell carcinoma through a TLR4-associated ERK/CD155/TIGIT signaling axis. The work links oral microbial dysbiosis to immune evasion in OSCC, suggesting a mechanistic pathway by which periodontal infection could contribute to cancer progression.

papers.title: Modulation of microbiota by traditional Chinese medicine in chronic inflammatory airway disease: a systematic review and meta-analysis of animal studies.
papers.abstract: A growing number of studies have indicated that traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) can regulate microbiota in chronic inflammatory airway disease (CIAD). Nevertheless, no systematic review or integrated analysis has summarized relevant evidence to date, limiting the clinical application of TCM in this field.
papers.summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis aggregates animal studies examining whether traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) modulates the gut or airway microbiota in chronic inflammatory airway diseases such as asthma and COPD. It provides the first integrated synthesis of this evidence base, aiming to clarify the microbiota-mediated mechanisms of TCM and support its clinical translation.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence-based tongue image analysis for non-invasive screening of gastric cancer, precancerous lesions, and related gastrointestinal disorders: a systematic review.
papers.abstract: Gastric cancer remains a major cause of cancer-related mortality, largely because many cases are diagnosed at an advanced stage. Upper gastrointestinal endoscopy with histopathological confirmation is the diagnostic gold standard, but its invasiveness, cost, and limited accessibility restrict population-level use. Artificial intelligence (AI)-based tongue-image analysis may provide an objective, low-cost, and non-invasive adjunct for pre-endoscopic risk stratification.
papers.summary: This systematic review examines whether AI-based analysis of tongue images can serve as a non-invasive screening tool for gastric cancer, precancerous lesions, and related gastrointestinal disorders. The authors argue that such an approach could offer a low-cost adjunct to endoscopy for pre-endoscopic risk stratification, though the abstract does not report pooled performance metrics. The review highlights the potential of tongue-image AI while noting the need for validation before population-level use.

papers.title: The hormone-microbiota-NET framework in gynecologic diseases: evidence, controversies, and translational opportunities.
papers.abstract: Gynecologic diseases, including infectious disorders, endocrine-related conditions, gynecologic malignancies, and pregnancy complications, are clinically diverse yet frequently share features of hormonal imbalance, microbial dysbiosis, and dysregulated inflammation. Current research has largely examined these processes separately, limiting integrated understanding of their potential interactions. This review synthesizes current evidence and proposes a hormone-microbiota-neutrophil extracellular trap (NET) framework as a conceptual tool for understanding common and disease-specific mechanisms a
papers.summary: This review synthesizes evidence linking hormonal imbalance, microbial dysbiosis, and neutrophil extracellular trap (NET) dysregulation across diverse gynecologic diseases, proposing a unified hormone-microbiota-NET conceptual framework. It highlights shared and disease-specific mechanisms while discussing controversies and translational opportunities for integrated therapeutic approaches.

papers.title: New insights into the gut-heart axis: microbial metabolite biomarkers, multi-omics, and engineered bacterial delivery systems.
papers.abstract: Despite rapid growth in gut-heart axis research, clinical translation remains limited. This review addresses that gap by critically synthesizing recent evidence on microbiota-derived metabolites, biomarkers, multi-omics workflows, and engineered bacterial interventions in cardiovascular disease (CVD). We examine how TMAO, short-chain fatty acids, bile acids, indole derivatives, and phenylacetylglutamine exert context-dependent cardiovascular effects, and why functional microbial gene markers and integrated biomarker panels may outperform single-taxon signatures. We then evaluate multi-omics st
papers.summary: This review synthesizes evidence on the gut-heart axis, examining how microbiota-derived metabolites such as TMAO, short-chain fatty acids, bile acids, indole derivatives, and phenylacetylglutamine influence cardiovascular disease in context-dependent ways. It argues that functional microbial gene markers and integrated biomarker panels may outperform single-taxon signatures, and evaluates multi-omics workflows alongside engineered bacterial delivery systems as emerging translational strategies.

papers.title: Decoding host-microbiome interactions through integrative multi-omics and artificial intelligence: from biological mechanisms to predictive modelling.
papers.abstract: The mutual communication between the human host and its microbiome plays a fundamental role in maintaining metabolic and immunological homeostasis. Disruptions in this delicate ecosystem are heavily linked to severe pathologies like inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), metabolic syndromes, and cancer. Whilst traditional single-omics approaches offer limited taxonomic snapshots, multi-omics strategies are bridging the gap by mapping the complex, multi-layered networks driving host-microbe interactions. However, integrating these highly dimensional, heterogeneous datasets creates significant comput
papers.summary: This review examines how combining multiple omics data types (genomics, transcriptomics, metabolomics, etc.) with artificial intelligence can illuminate the complex bidirectional interactions between the human host and its microbiome. It argues that multi-omics integration overcomes the limited taxonomic snapshots of single-omics approaches, enabling mapping of multi-layered networks underlying conditions like IBD, metabolic syndrome, and cancer. The paper also discusses computational challenges in integrating highly dimensional, heterogeneous datasets and the path toward predictive modelling.

papers.title: Global perspectives on dietary management of small intestinal bacterial overgrowth (SIBO): a systematic review of clinical guidelines, consensus statements and expert recommendations.
papers.abstract: Small intestinal bacterial overgrowth (SIBO) is a disorder associated with gastrointestinal symptoms, alterations in gut microbiota composition, and a high rate of recurrence. Although antibiotic therapy remains the cornerstone of treatment, dietary interventions are increasingly used as adjunctive strategies to improve symptom control and support long-term management. However, international recommendations regarding dietary management remain heterogeneous and lack standardization. Therefore, the aim of this systematic review was to analyze and compare dietary recommendations for the treatment
papers.summary: This systematic review compares international clinical guidelines, consensus statements, and expert recommendations for dietary management of small intestinal bacterial overgrowth (SIBO). The authors find that dietary recommendations are heterogeneous and lack standardization across sources, despite growing use of dietary interventions as adjuncts to antibiotic therapy. The work highlights the need for harmonized guidance in this area.

papers.title: Biliary microbiota and metabolic reprogramming in gallstone-associated gallbladder cancer: evidence from bile, stones, mucosa and tumor tissue.
papers.abstract: Gallbladder cancer (GBC) commonly arises in gallbladders affected by cholelithiasis and chronic cholecystitis, although malignancy develops in only a small minority of patients with stones. This disparity has directed attention to the local conditions created by concentrated bile, stone surfaces, persistent microbes and altered bile acid and lipid metabolism. Evidence in this field is difficult to compare because bile, stones, mucosa and tumor tissue measure different biological processes, while human associations, animal experiments and cross-sectional omics studies are often discussed togeth
papers.summary: This review examines how the biliary microbiota and metabolic changes (particularly bile acid and lipid metabolism) may contribute to gallbladder cancer arising in the context of gallstones and chronic cholecystitis. It highlights that evidence from bile, stones, mucosa, and tumor tissue reflects different biological processes and is often conflated across human, animal, and cross-sectional omics studies, complicating interpretation. The paper synthesizes this literature and likely calls for more standardized, compartment-specific approaches.
